gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Approachable and clean, Noto Sans Sunuwar leaves daylight in its curves and keeps its ascender stems short. Junegull, with no thick-and-thin modulation at all, sets that against solid retro letters, and long paragraphs should feel easy on the eye.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-syloti-: Clean and friendly, this pairing splits its jobs. Junegull gives retro display letters with closed shapes, while Noto Syloti Nagri keeps ascenders short and the a open at the bottom.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-syriac-: Modern and clean, Noto Sans Syriac Western holds its terminals far from the stroke body, with small letters packed like bundled cable. Junegull's line never changes weight, so a long page of the body stays steady.

gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Junegull has no thick-and-thin modulation whatsoever. Noto Sans Tai Le lets its ink strokes taper out before touching and keeps the step from capital to lowercase minimal, so the two sit easily together on a page.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-tai-tha: Junegull traces its letters as if with one marker. Noto Sans Tai Tham has chalk-board lowercase crowding the capital line and open c shapes, so extended reading stays clear and contemporary.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-tai-vie: Junegull is retro and rounded, with a lowercase of cast-iron stature. Noto Sans Tai Viet pulls its terminals back from each curve and keeps ascenders short, so the heading's closed forms meet open, approachable text.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-tamil-s: Round forms like open parentheses give the body a stocky, contemporary look, thanks to a very big middle band. Noto Sans Tamil Supplement is the clear partner to Junegull's outlined, one-width letters.
